analysis: Examined base-side units of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (base lines 956-1467). This is a documentation-only change. Head changes per the range map: date bump (line 3); new Swift-only optional `detail` field on the model_autopilot status (head 854), which carries a busy reason or `autopilot_operation` and is diagnostic only; new Swift-only `hold_seconds` command field (head 1208), described as a 0...86400 placement hold that requires load_model_id, otherwise `invalid_command`; edits around head 1355-1380, i.e. the model_autopilot state table, where busy-reason docs likely sit; and the Related/tests section (head 1470-1472). The base line 1442 change in the Model unloading section is also noted. These describe provider-local residency and autopilot metadata. They add no trust grant, encryption, attestation or billing semantics. The visible excerpt says older coordinators ignore `detail`. The doc claims `hold_seconds` is bounded like lease_seconds, and the excerpt is truncated. No threat-model asset (A-001, A-003, A-016) or boundary (TB-002, TB-011) is affected by documented behavior, and the T-041 cache-receipt sections are unchanged. Implementation source for hold_seconds and the busy detail was not supplied. Integration should confirm that the Swift implementation bounds hold_seconds, keeps it within the selected-model allowlist and live-lease gating (ModelAutopilotPolicy.swift), and does not let the `detail` text leak sensitive state. This is an availability-only concern.
